svg.title: Chat streaming — POST /chat, detached generation, SSE frames, stop and re-attach

g.text: Chat streaming — POST /chat, detached generation, SSE frames, stop and re-attach

(evidence: orchestrator/app/main.py:274-796 · orchestrator/app/sse.py:34-54 · orchestrator/app/llm.py:215-262 · frontend/lib/streams.ts:82-393 · frontend/lib/sse.ts:126-301 · frontend/app/api/chat/route.ts:123-185)
Trust boundary — orchestrator :8080 published on 0.0.0.0, ZERO authentication
body, then JSON.stringify makes a second copy (chat/route.ts:126, :154-166).
Images and PDFs travel as base64
this body and there is no size
cap on either side — the orchestrator installs only CORSMiddleware
(main.py:47-53). The streaming fix exists for /api/upload and was never
The `cookie` header is forwarded (chat/route.ts:160-162) but it is dead
code: current_user() deletes the Request and returns the one local row
Every hop in this diagram is unauthenticated.
so the 404 at main.py:343-344 is skipped (main.py:338-341). The comment
directly above it asserts the opposite behaviour.
db.connect() also re-runs the schema + migration on
(db.py:203-204), and this call is blocking inside an async def.
— sse.py:34-44 raises ValueError on anything else,
· `meta` data: engine keys merged with mode/model/effort/generation_id
Frame format is literally `event: <name>` NEWLINE `data: <json>` NEWLINE NEWLINE.
`meta` is the ONLY event parsed with
JSON.parse cast to Meta (sse.ts:202-203) — while `step` and `research`
are checked field by field (sse.ts:137-201). `meta` is exactly the event
that carries sql, data, chart and report_files into the UI.
Two live drifts: route "dataset" is missing from the frontend Engine union
(types.ts:8) and `auto` is missing from interface Meta (main.py:378-379).
[gen.subscribers == 0 — nobody was attached at the end]
: no log, no retry, no client signal.
follow() decrements `subscribers` in a finally (main.py:119-120), so an
abandoned async generator whose aclose() is deferred keeps subscribers > 0
frame: finish() makes follow() break (main.py:114-115) and the socket just
closes. sse.py:20-24 documents `done` and `error` as the only terminals;
streams.ts:264-268 silently maps the frameless close to status 'done'.
The caller fire-and-forgets with a catch that returns undefined
(streams.ts:91) and never inspects {stopped}, so a stop that fails leaves
_owns()/_viewer_id() (main.py:693-709) compare one local identity to itself.
4 · Re-attach after reload or tab switch
[a generation is still live and _owns(gen, viewer)]
frame is retained for the whole life of the generation purely so a
re-attach can replay it. No cap, no eviction, one buffer per concurrent
conversation, and lifespan() has no shutdown branch to drain them
Any uncaught exception in worker() → publish("error", {"message": str(exc)})
unsanitised and is never logged. If the stream raises *after* tokens were
emitted, `meta` never fires (chat.py:104) and the client is left holding a
partial answer with no meta, then an `error`.
Every non-2xx from /api/chat — including a 400 and a 502 wrapping an
upstream 422 — is flattened to "The orchestrator is unreachable."
No timeout bounds worker() as a whole.
The only bound is the per-call
httpx LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 300 s (config.py:264, llm.py:78). There is **no
keep-alive/heartbeat frame** and no `id:`/`retry:` field in sse.py, so a
long silent generation depends entirely on X-Accel-Buffering: no and on no
intermediary having an idle timeout. sse.ts has no idle detection either —
No retry exists anywhere on this path.
Solid arrow = request · dashed arrow = response/stream.
Amber note = unbounded resource or timeout gap.
Red note = swallowed error, fail-open or unauthenticated hop.
Every arrow is labelled protocol · payload · sync|async.
